newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Dec 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Dec 27.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- FORMER FINANCIAL ADVISER TO CONTEST CRITICS' CLAIMS

Knight Williams, the former financial adviser at the centre of the pensions mis-selling scandal, is hitting back against its critics. It plans to write to other members of the financial services industry, reminding them they stand to pay the bill for the affair via an Investors Compensation Scheme levy. It will also argue that a report into the affair shows that many of the investors that the Securities and Investments Board said had a case for receiving compensation would not successfully argue their cases in court.
-- GEORGE SAYS FURTHER INTEREST RATE RISES WILL BE NECESSARY

Bank of England Governor Eddie George has said in an interview with French newspaper Le Figaro that a rise in interest rates will be necessary at some point. He said this was needed due to rising consumption, shown by 'strong growth' in the money supply. He was also quoted as attacking the Maastricht Treaty as too restrictive, given the realities of European economies.

-- EXPORT SURGE SLASHES TRADE GAP A strong surge in exports to Germany and France helped halve Britain's trade gap in October to the lowest level since early 1995. Office of National Statistics figures showed the strong growth in exports to the rest of the European Union helped cut the trade deficit with the rest of the world to a seasonally adjusted 454 million pounds stg.
-- NORTHERN BID OPPONENTS MAY HOLD OUT

Leading minority shareholders in Northern Electric have not yet decided whether to accept the 782 million pound stg takeover bid from CalEnergy. 50.3 per cent of Northern shares have been approved, and the board is expected to recommend that minority shareholders accept the bid. However, speculation surrounded several shareholders, such as M&G and Foreign and Colonial, who may decide to remain minority shareholders, due to the potential value of dividends.
-- LAPORTE'S EUROPEAN ADHESIVES SOLD TO ELF ATOCHEM

UK specialty chemicals company Laporte has sold its European adhesives business to Elf Atochem for about 100 million pounds stg. The deal is part of a radical restructuring of the Laporte operation by Jim Leng, who became chief executive one year ago and is likely to see other divisions sold.
-- SPAIN DISRUPTS TELEFONICA'S PLANS TO CONTROL SUBSIDIARY

Spanish telecoms group Telefonica's plans to take full control of its Latin American subsidiary have been disrupted by the decision by the Spanish government to seek maximum price for its stake. However, the final stage of Telefonica's own privatisation is likely to go ahead, with the government due to sell its 21 per cent stake to the parent group in February.
-- WISEMAN RECEIVES CLEARANCE TO BID

Robert Wiseman Dairies is to discuss a possible takeover of main competitor Scottish Pride Holdings after a government go-ahead. The two hold about 80 per cent of the Scottish milk market. Under the conditions of the approval, the company must give undertakings to the Office of Fair Trading about prices and acquisitions.
-- NEWS CORP MAY OFFER 30 PER CENT OF ASKYB

News Corporation is considering a 30 per cent public offer of American Sky Broadcasting, the digital satellite television venture due to be launched next year. The original partner in the project, MCI Communications, is now in the process of merging with British Telecom.
-- YAMAICHI TO BAIL OUT LENDING AFFILIATE

Yamaichi Securities, the weakest of Japan's big four stockbrokers, is to inject 150 billion yen into affiliate Yamaichi to write off bad property loans. The move is part of a campaign by the leading stockbrokers to clear the damage caused by the collapse of property prices five years ago.
-- TEXACO IN 600 MILLION DOLLAR CHEMICALS DISPOSAL

Texaco has agreed to sell the remainder of its chemicals business to Huntsman Corporation of the US for about 600 million dollars.
